title: Khaman Dhokla
subtitle: Soft, spongy steamed besan cake leavened with Eno, soaked in a sweet mustard-seed tempering.

method.title: Make the batter
items: Pour {@water:batter} into a bowl; add {@ginger}, {@salt}, {@sugar}, {@oil:batter} and {@lemon}
Stir well until the sugar dissolves; keep aside
Set a sieve over a large mixing bowl; sieve {@besan} and {@turmeric} into it, then mix in {@semolina}
Pour in the wet mix and whisk to a smooth, lump-free, flowing batter
Bring {@steam-water} to a boil in a steamer or wide pot with a stand; grease a 7–8 inch tin with {@oil:grease}

method.label: Toddler — her mini dhokla (before the green chili)
items: Spoon {=3 tbsp} of plain batter into a small greased katori — it steams beside the big tin

method.title: Leaven and steam
items: Sprinkle {@eno} over the batter, pour {@water:eno} on top to activate it and stir gently in one direction until frothy — about 10 seconds; stir a pinch of the frothy batter into her katori too
Pour straight into the greased tin and place it, with her katori, in the steamer
Cover and steam on medium-high 15–18 min (her katori: 10–12 min), until a toothpick comes out clean
Rest 5 min, then cut into squares

method.title: Tempering
items: Heat {@oil-temper} in a small pan; add {@mustard} and let them splutter
Add {@hing}, {@curry-leaves} and {@slit-chilies}; fry a few seconds
Add {@water-temper}, {@sugar-temper} and {@salt-temper}; bring to a boil and turn off
Spoon it evenly over the dhokla squares and let them soak 5 min; serve with green chutney

method.label: Tip
method.text: Add the Eno only when the steamer is boiling and the tin is greased — it loses its lift within a minute. Her katori skips the chili: give her the soft dhokla with a drizzle of the tempering water, without chili pieces. Swap the lemon for ⅓ tsp citric acid if you like.
